transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, um, I guess I'm here because of how I've been eating. What really made me come in today is that once I start eating a certain way, it feels like I hit some kind of switch. I just keep going, even while part of me is in the background thinking, you know, Dennis, just stop already. But I just keep eating.
Can you describe what you mean by 'keep going'—is it more that you feel unable to stop eating once you start, or is it that you continue eating even though you're no longer hungry?

Yeah, it's definitely that I feel unable to stop. Like I was just saying, it's... it's like I lose control of it. I'll be sitting there, fully aware that I should quit, telling myself to just put the food down, but I just can't make myself do it. I just keep reaching for more anyway.
After these episodes of eating where you feel like you can't stop, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up or take anything like laxatives. And I definitely don't exercise a bunch afterward. I just... I just feel really bad about it, but I don't do anything to try and undo it, if that makes sense.
Can you tell me if these episodes of not being able to stop eating happen within a specific, limited period of time—like a couple of hours—or does it feel more spread out over the day?

It usually happens in a pretty short window, yeah. Like, maybe an hour or two. It usually happens on nights after a big project deadline for one of my classes, or if my roommates leave leftover pizza out in the apartment. I'll just take it to my room, and before I know it, I'll eat an entire small pizza, plus a bag of chips, and then a big bowl of cereal. It's way more than I ever plan to eat, and definitely way more than what my roommates would eat for a normal dinner. It just all happens at once, really fast.
